papers.summary: Spectral weight decay reduces weight effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss in 124M–500M LLaMA models. The inspected paper also reports that applying it during short fine-tuning incurs substantially more loss at the same rank.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses training for low-rank compressibility, nuclear-norm regularization, and label noise.

evidence.quote: spectral weight decay lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss.
Within the observed overlap, fine-tuning incurs substantially more loss at the same rank.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: Analyzes how GD, SignGD, Muon, Shampoo, and K-FAC change the emergence and decay of singular modes in deep matrix factorization.
papers.relevance: Directly informs the question of how optimizer geometry shapes spectral bias, although its analysis uses a simplified model.

evidence.quote: Under explicit balance and alignment assumptions, we derive birth, saturation, and decay laws for Euclidean GD, coordinate-wise updates of SignGD and an instantaneous Adam approximation, spectral updates of Muon and cumulative Shampoo, and a block curvature model of K-FAC.

papers.title: Optimizer Geometry Sets the Pace: Spectral Learning Dynamics in Matrix Factorization

papers.summary: Uses targeted orthogonalization to probe which momentum singular directions matter in Muon. NanoGPT diagnostics distinguish weight-spectrum flattening from validation-loss improvement.
papers.relevance: Matches the interests in Muon, Newton–Schulz approximation, and effective rank of training matrices.

evidence.quote: the bottom targeted variants keep Muon’s rank without matching its loss, and full-spectrum updates keep the spectrum flat for free.

papers.title: Spectrally Targeted Muon

papers.summary: Defines a behavioral compression rate for LoRA adapters and finds that compression difficulty depends on the dataset–base-model pair. Correction spectra rank rates within some receivers but do not transfer reliably across receivers.
papers.relevance: Connects low-rank update spectra to whether compressed fine-tuning preserves acquired behavior.

evidence.quote: Behavioral rate therefore depends on the dataset–receiver pair, rather than on the dataset alone.
This association does not transfer reliably across receivers.

papers.title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information

papers.summary: Adds an SVD-free Rényi-2 effective-rank regularizer to LoRA fine-tuning. The reported mixed-domain rank sweeps show lower mean Wiki perplexity at tested ranks of at least 16, with configuration-dependent learning–retention trade-offs.
papers.relevance: Tests whether explicitly shaping adapter rank improves practical language-model fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: a penalty weight of λ = 0.01 lowers mean Wiki perplexity at every tested rank of at least 16 relative to unpenalized LoRA.
Single-task and scheduling experiments further show that the balance between learning and retention depends on the configuration.

papers.title: Maximizing Capacity Utilization of LoRA Adapters for Mitigating the Learning-Forgetting Trade-off

papers.summary: Measures LoRA’s rank-dependent second descent under label noise against module-matched dense fine-tuning. In the tested 7B language-model sweep, the LoRA–dense test-NLL gap remains positive at every measured rank.
papers.relevance: Directly joins LoRA rank, memorization under noisy labels, and generalization.

evidence.quote: G remains positive at every measured rank and in every seed, parity included.
The dense reference is module-matched, training the projections LoRA adapts rather than the whole network

papers.title: LoRA's Second Descent Extends Beyond Parameter Parity

papers.summary: Tracks drifting low-rank gradient subspaces during LLaMA pretraining. At rank 32 in the inspected 1B setup, reported optimizer-step peak memory is 0.2487 GB for Ori versus 0.3385 GB for GaLore.
papers.relevance: A direct GaLore-style candidate for memory-efficient LLM pretraining.

evidence.quote: at rank 32, Ori requires only 0.2487 GB, which is 12.1% less than OSD (0.2832 GB) and 26.5% less than GaLore (0.3385 GB).
Our goal is to record the peak memory usage, incurred solely by the said optimizer’s update step.

papers.title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training

papers.summary: Uses Nyström sketches and a quantized variant to reduce optimizer-state memory in LLaMA pretraining. In the inspected 1.3B comparison, Q-Clean reports 1.28 GB optimizer memory and 50.24 GB peak memory, versus Muon’s 2.80 GB and 51.83 GB.
papers.relevance: Provides measured quality–memory–wall-clock trade-offs for low-rank optimizer-state compression.

evidence.quote: Clean reaches AdamW’s final performance in 64 hours instead of 81

papers.title: Clean: Second-order LLM Training at Linear Memory Cost via Nystr{ö}m Sketching

papers.summary: Combines Monarch-factor weights with Muon. Inspected systems measurements show lower peak memory and full-step time than dense Muon at larger reference sizes, but those measurements are separate from complete quality runs.
papers.relevance: Addresses how structured parameterization changes training memory, optimizer cost, and throughput with model width.

evidence.quote: At 6.89B, Monarch–Muon reduces the full-step time by 45% and peak memory by 23% relative to dense Muon.
The systems experiments measure training operations on larger reference architectures, separately from the complete quality runs in Appendix A.1 .

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: CORE is a training-free deep-research harness that retrieves broad passages but returns selected snippets, with source expansion and deduplication. Controlled closed-search comparisons report higher answer accuracy and evidence recall than two comparator harnesses.
papers.relevance: Directly informs retrieval and context management in a handwritten research-digest agent.

evidence.quote: CORE retrieves whole passages to judge relevance, then reuses the reranker’s token-level similarities to return only the most relevant snippet from each one.
Across three agent models and three benchmarks, CORE achieves higher answer accuracy and evidence recall than Tongyi DeepResearch and OpenResearcher in every model–benchmark comparison

papers.title: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research

limitations: These are paper-reported claims, not independently reproduced results.
Ori’s quoted memory metric measures additional optimizer-step allocation, not total training peak memory.
Monarch-Muon’s large-scale systems measurements are separate from its complete quality runs; projection-refresh timings for comparison methods are excluded.
CORE was evaluated in closed search, not specifically on a paper-digest corpus.
No X-attention inference was made because X analysis is disabled.
